notes: Summary: enterprise RAG/search vendor looking to replace homegrown FAISS clusters; primary driver = cost + operational complexity at 100M-1B vector scale.
Workloads: heavy embeddings creation (batch offline + streaming updates), primary read pattern = dense retrieval + cross-encoder reranking on top 100 candidates.
Performance targets: 99th pctile end-to-end <150ms for simple search (retrieve+light reranker), preferred 50-80ms for cached hot-path queries; peak QPS target 2k across shard set.
Scale expectations: start POC at 100M vectors; roadmap to 500M in 6 months and 1B+ within 12-18 months.
Cost sensitivity: target unit cost per query < $0.0008 for retrieve+rerank at production scale; strong interest in batching, prefix/KV cache, and quantization to hit targets.
Model preferences: open embeddings models (6B-ish) for bulk embedding; small cross-encoder reranker (distil or re-ranked distilled model) to reduce reranker CPU/GPU cost.
Routing/fallback: want automatic fallback to cheaper model variants when load spikes; can tolerate slightly lower recall on fallback for non-critical queries.
Security: must support SSO/SAML, audit logs forwarded to their Splunk stack, retention controls for PII, and option for on-prem private deployments for regulated customers.
Quote from Head of Search: 'We can’t afford to have our index cost scale linearly with vector count — need clear unit economics and autoscaling that doesn’t blow up our OPEX.'
Ingestion notes: currently use nightly ETL to produce new vectors; primary concerns are sustained ingest throughput and re-sharding costs; want bulk import + delta streaming.
Technical asks: support for IVF+PQ or HNSW+PQ on disk, incremental index building, online rebalancing, and checkpointed uploads for big bulk loads.

POC success criteria: 1) ingest 100M vectors within 72 hours, 2) maintain 95th pctile retrieval latency <40ms (retrieve-only), 3) end-to-end rerank latency <150ms at 500 QPS mixed traffic, 4) projected per-query cost below threshold in cost-model report.
Open risks: KMS key policy mapping to Redwood-managed infra, network egress/residency constraints for EU customers, and existing vendor lock with Elastic for some SKUs.
Internal notes (AE): pricing sensitive; likely wants a 12–24 month committed Reserved/Dedicated contract if POC numbers look good.
Ask for SE: prepare two POC configs — high-throughput (batch ingest + sharded index) and low-latency (replicated hot set + KV cache); include quantization tradeoffs.
Linked artifacts: security FAQ (drive:/security/tesseract/security-faq.pdf), pricing proposal v2 (drive:/deals/tesseract/pricing-proposal-v2.pptx).
Next immediate step: schedule engineering-run with Redwood infra team week of 2026-03-08 to kick off 100M ingest trial.
